gl.afterArticle:
After Hours — Gabriele Lucia / oakvx

The channel for what stays open after I log off.

About me

After hours I write code with no particular purpose, mostly because I like figuring out how things work. Sometimes I rebuild something from scratch even though it already worked, simply because I have since found a better way. My computer stays on a little longer than it should. That is usually how it goes.

Four things I keep open after I log off:

  • Free time — Personal projects. They usually start with a small idea and end up becoming real tools, with a few more features than they needed.
  • Details — Interfaces. I adjust colours, spacing and small movements until the code and graphics feel like they came from the same person.
  • Languages — Italian, English, Spanish and Greek. One native language and three I have practised at different times, for different reasons.
  • Curiosity — One question leads to another. I start with a simple question about how something works and end up reading far more than I needed to.

Status: one more small refinement · online. When an idea really grabs me, I see it through.

Projects

A few more projects: three ideas I started to learn something, developed far enough to deserve pages of their own.

  • Brat Animator (Canvas, JavaScript) — a browser editor that turns LRC lyrics into animated lyric videos.
  • Synk (Node.js) — starts with a chat, understands the reason for a message and connects appointments and business data to Google Calendar and a dashboard.
  • Beautify (PHP + MySQL, diploma project) — a multi-salon management system for customers, services, appointments and availability.

Consoles

The consoles I have modified: three Nintendo 3DS systems, Wii U, Wii and PlayStation 4.

Games

  • Rayman Legends — one of my favourite games.
  • Yo-kai Watch 2: Bony Spirits — I like the whole series, but the second game is my favourite.
  • Just Dance 2017 — I like them all, but this is the one I am most attached to.

Languages

Write to me in your language: this opens a ready-made email in the language you choose, and I will reply in the same one. Italian (native), English C1, Spanish B1, Greek B1 and Chinese A2.

After hours I write code with no particular purpose, mostly because I like figuring out how things work. Sometimes I rebuild something that already worked, simply because I have found a better way. Languages work much the same: I use English every day, put my Spanish to the test while living in Seville for a while, and picked up Greek out of curiosity.

Fuera de horario escribo código que no tiene un propósito concreto, sobre todo porque me gusta entender cómo funcionan las cosas. Con los idiomas pasa algo parecido: uso inglés todos los días, puse a prueba mi español viviendo una temporada en Sevilla, y aprendí griego por curiosidad.

Εκτός ωραρίου γράφω κώδικα χωρίς συγκεκριμένο σκοπό, κυρίως επειδή μου αρέσει να καταλαβαίνω πώς λειτουργούν τα πράγματα. Με τις γλώσσες γίνεται κάτι παρόμοιο: χρησιμοποιώ αγγλικά κάθε μέρα, δοκίμασα τα ισπανικά μου ζώντας για ένα διάστημα στη Σεβίλλη, και έμαθα ελληνικά από περιέργεια.

Get in touch: Italiano · English · Español · Ελληνικά

GitHub

Commits, from day one. Public commits attributed to @oakvx and @oakvxish.

Tools

Three areas of work. Web development: websites and applications, interfaces, publishing and search visibility; HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SEO; websites for garages, beauty salons and hardware shops from 2023 to 2026. Backend and data: Node.js, PHP, PostgreSQL, MySQL and T-SQL on SQL Server; Synk, Beautify and Format SRL. Graphics and interfaces: social content, interface design and animated Canvas text; Brat Animator and social pages.

Based in Sassuolo, in the province of Modena. Studying Computer Engineering at the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia (UNIMORE). Abroad: May and June 2025, an Erasmus+ placement at Starbotica in Seville, with IT support and educational activities in English and Spanish. Contact: gabrielelucia07@gmail.com.

Curiosity

Word of the day: ταξίδι (taxídi, journey). I start with a simple question about how something works and end up reading far more than I needed to.
